scope: Serialize the bounded ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY object-ID list in the low-level DXF writer when every source handle resolves to a nonzero final output identity and each DWG handle role has a supported DXF group-code mapping.

behavior: The writer preflights the complete ordered object-ID list before emitting the proxy record, requires an installed resolver, bounds the list, rejects unsupported DWG handle codes and mismatched stored DXF group codes, and refuses zero, sentinel, or wider-than-32-bit source/output handles.
The DWG parser and DXF writer now share one handle-code-to-group mapping. Tolerant parsing retains the prior group-330 fallback for unknown codes, while strict output refuses them.

Resolved references are emitted in source order before group 94. Mappings exercised include DWG codes 4→DXF 330, 5→340, 2→350, 3→360, and 6/8/10/12→330; the DXF representation preserves the pointer/owner group role but canonicalizes those DWG soft-pointer encoding codes to group 330.

The explicit resolver overload is scoped to proxy object-ID edges; an independently configured global resolver remains unchanged and does not rewrite these groups. It provides an adapter integration point for a bounded source-graph mapping without changing common-reference behavior for other records.
Resolver output is treated as a final emitted handle and is not remapped again. The resolver is caller-supplied; this does not prove that its targets exist or have the required graph roles.
The dwg2dxf adapter still has no complete proxy-reference graph resolver and remains fail-closed for nonempty proxy object-ID lists.

validationProfile.source: Locally authored DRW_ProxyEntity records and resolver mappings. No DWG/DXF fixtures were added.
assertions: Typed readback preserves the ordered 330/340/350/360/330 groups and their final mapped handles.
A conflicting global resolver does not alter the explicit per-proxy mapping.
A missing resolver target, mismatched handle-role/group-code pair, unsupported DWG handle code, and wider-than-32-bit source handle each refuse atomically and preserve an existing destination.
Correcting the mapping and then the role succeeds through the same writer and adapter; caller-side source handles and the original ordered reference list remain unchanged.
The existing adapter-level no-resolver refusal and corrected no-reference retry continue to pass.

validation.fixturePolicy: No DWG/DXF fixture files were added or committed.

authorities.title: Autodesk ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY DXF reference
authorities.use: Defines the optional repeated object-ID group codes 330, 340, 350, and 360 and group 94 as the end of the object-ID list.

authorities.title: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, §20.4.90
authorities.use: Identifies the proxy's trailing object IDs as typed object handles; the implementation reuses libdxfrw's existing parser role mapping and does not claim the specification independently proves graph closure.

limitations: Generated low-level serializer/readback evidence only; no physical DWG source-to-output, independent consumer, or native proxy semantics qualification.
The resolver is trusted to return a correct final output identity. The writer does not verify target existence, target type, ownership, recursive dependencies, or target emission.
dwg2dxf does not configure this resolver, so physical conversion remains fail-closed for these references until source-bound graph planning and output binding are implemented.
Unknown-data slots, EED/common references, mixed class/ACDS graphs, and other unsupported proxy profiles remain refused. No support claim is promoted.
